title: Cocktail 2 Has Crossed ₹60 Crore. So Why Is the Whole Trade Whispering About an Asterisk?
excerpt: Shahid, Kriti and Rashmika's glossy love triangle looks like a winner on paper. Look closer and the numbers tell a quieter, more complicated story.
body:
There is a version of the **Cocktail 2** story that is pure summer-blockbuster fairy tale. A 4-star verdict from Taran Adarsh on day one. A ₹8.83 crore advance. Sicily glittering on screen, a Pritam album already living rent-free on every road-trip playlist, and a cume that sailed past ₹60 crore by Wednesday. Shahid Kapoor back in romantic-lead mode. Kriti Sanon firing up the screen. Rashmika Mandanna in her first big Bollywood-machine spotlight.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=XXxUqLHq1xg</youtube>

And then there is the version the trade is actually talking about — in lowered voices, with a raised eyebrow.

https://x.com/DrDatta_AIIMS/status/2069714026725331375

Because six days in, **Cocktail 2** has done ₹60.50 crore nett, and almost nobody who watches these numbers for a living believes that figure is telling the whole truth.

> "Its numbers should be taken with an asterisk." — Pinkvilla box office analysis, Day 6

That is an unusually blunt thing to say about a film that, on the surface, is performing. Day 6 brought in ₹4.50 crore, a roughly 20 percent drop from the day before — the kind of weekday hold that looks fine until you ask *what* is holding it up. The honest answer, per multiple trade desks, is external push: bulk and block bookings, corporate support, the machinery that can make a first week look healthy without a single extra real ticket-buyer walking in off the street. The film is heading toward roughly ₹64 crore for week one. Pretty, but propped.

Here is the tell. The original **Cocktail**, back in 2012, opened to a modest ₹10.50 crore and *grew* — legging its way to ₹74.50 crore nett on pure word-of-mouth, the way the best romantic dramas always have. **Cocktail 2** front-loaded its money and is now leaking it. The sequel will very likely cross the original's lifetime total. As Pinkvilla put it, with a shrug you can almost hear: "that will hardly matter."

What does matter is the production cost, which is steep, which quietly reclassifies a ₹60-crore-and-counting "hit" into something closer to an average performer dressed in designer clothes. It will *look* better than this year's other rom-com casualties — *Hai Jawani Toh Ishq Hona Hai*, *Pati Patni Aur Woh Do* — but looking better than the floor is not the same as flying.

None of which is the film's fault, exactly. By most accounts **Cocktail 2** is a genuinely good-looking, good-sounding movie. **Homi Adajania**, who made the 2012 original, returns to the same emotional terrain — three people, two of whom are in love, one of whom is in trouble — and dresses it in expensive light. Shahid plays Kunal. Kriti is Ally, the live-wire "mashooqa." Rashmika is Diya, the calmer gravity at the centre. **Sanjay Dutt** anchors the older generation. The cinematography is glossy to the point of indulgence; the Sicilian coastline does half the romancing. "Tujhko," the Arijit Singh ache between Shahid and Rashmika, is the kind of song that outlives the film it came from. "Jag Se Laaj" gives Kriti a dance-floor moment she clearly relishes.

So why the asterisk anxiety? Because the trade has watched this trick before, and it has learned to separate the spectacle of an opening from the truth of a second week. The real test, as one analyst noted, begins the moment the makers stop helping the numbers and let the film fare organically — which, so far, "seems unlikely."

**For the diaspora**, the math is more forgiving and the experience more straightforward. **Cocktail 2** is playing across US, UK, Canada and Gulf multiplexes right now — AMC and Cinemark in the States, Cineworld and Vue in the UK — and overseas audiences tend to reward exactly this kind of glossy, music-led romance regardless of what the Mumbai trade thinks of its booking strategy. An OTT date hasn't been announced, but going by the Maddock-Vijan playbook, expect a Netflix landing roughly eight weeks out.

Here is the honest take: see it for the songs, the stars and the Sicily of it all. Just know that when someone tells you **Cocktail 2** is a "₹60-crore hit," the number is real and the word is doing a lot of heavy lifting. The film didn't need the asterisk. The strategy gave it one anyway.
author: Diaspora Desk
